jobs.occupation: Part time Employee within the Field of Post-quantum Cryptography - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
Implementation and security analysis of quantum-secure anonymous credentials (part-time, January–May 2027)

Would you like to spend five months working on cryptography that protects people’s privacy, also against future quantum computers? 

We are looking for a motivated part time employee with a Bachelor’s degree to join the cryptography research team in the Cybersecurity Engineering section at DTU Compute from January to May 2027.

Anonymous credentials allow people to prove something about themselves, for example that they are over 18 or hold a valid licence, without revealing who they are. The schemes in use today would be broken by a large-scale quantum computer. In our project, we build anonymous credentials that remain secure in a post-quantum world, and you will help us turn this research into working code and a scientific publication.

The job
You will become part of our cryptography research team, which consists of 4 faculty members and 7 PhD students. We study the design, security and efficiency of cryptographic protocols, with a focus on post-quantum and privacy-enhancing cryptography. The project is led by Carsten Baum and Marvin Beckmann, and you will work primarily together with Marvin in your daily work.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Implement a post-quantum anonymous credential scheme and its cryptographic building blocks in software
• Test and benchmark the implementation, for example with respect to running times and credential sizes
• Contribute to the security analysis of the scheme, including the choice of concrete parameters
• Help write a scientific article that presents the results
• Take part in regular project meetings and discuss progress and ideas with the team
• Hold a Bachelor’s degree in computer science, mathematics, software technology, cybersecurity or a similar field, and are preferably enrolled in a Master’s programme
• Have taken one or more courses in cryptography and are comfortable with the underlying mathematics
• Have solid programming skills, preferably in a systems programming language such as Rust, C or C++
• Are interested in post-quantum cryptography, zero-knowledge proofs or privacy-enhancing technologies; prior experience with these topics is an advantage, but not a requirement
• Communicate well in written and spoken English
The position is part-time with approximately 10 hours per week. We plan the work together with you, so that it can be combined with your studies.

We imagine that you
As a person, you are curious and eager to learn new things. You work in a structured and independent way, ask questions when something is unclear, and enjoy collaborating with others in a research team. Experience with scientific writing, for example from a Bachelor’s thesis, is welcome.

What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international research environment. You will get hands-on experience with state-of-the-art cryptography and insight into how a research project goes from idea to publication. You will be closely supervised by researchers in the team, and the position is a good opportunity to find out whether research, for example a later Master’s thesis or PhD project in cryptography, is something for you.

We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism and a good working atmosphere, and we offer great flexibility in the position. In the area of technical and natural sciences, DTU is one of the leading research and education institutions in Europe.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an AC Bachelor. 

In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The position is a fixed-term, part-time position of approximately 10 hours per week for 5 months. 

Starting date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement), and the employment ends on 31 May 2027.

The workplace is DTU Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 10 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

You can read more about DTU Compute and the Cybersecurity Engineering section at www.compute.dtu.dk. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor, Carsten Baum by sending an e-mail to cabau@dtu.dk.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

jobs.description:
The Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen is seeking a research technician specialising in data analysis and data management to join the Stamou laboratory. The position is for six months, starting on 1 February 2027.

  About us
 The Department of Chemistry combines research and education across the molecular sciences, training bachelor’s, master’s and PhD students. The Stamou laboratory develops fluorescence microscopy methods to study the pharmacology and biophysical properties of membrane proteins at the nanoscale.

  Your job
 You will support the laboratory’s cell biology and microscopy activities by providing image analysis, quantitative data analysis and data management support. You will work closely with researchers to turn experimental measurements into well-documented results and maintain organised, accessible research datasets.

  Your tasks include:

  •   Process and quantitatively analyse microscopy images, including fluorescence images from cell biology experiments.

  •   Analyse experimental data, perform quality control and statistical analysis, and prepare figures and summaries for scientific interpretation.

  •   Organise and maintain image files, experimental datasets, metadata and analysis outputs, with clear documentation and traceable records.

  •   Help implement and improve reproducible analysis workflows and support consistent data storage, retrieval and sharing within the laboratory.

  Profile

  •   A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as data science, bioinformatics, physics, biophysics, computer science or the life sciences.

  •   Practical experience in quantitative data analysis and interpretation of experimental results.

  •   Experience in microscopy image analysis, including the use of relevant image-processing software.

  •   A systematic approach to data organisation, documentation and reproducible analysis. Experience with scientific programming or scripting is an advantage.

  •   Attention to detail, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and clear communication of methods and results to colleagues.

  We’re offering
 We offer the opportunity to apply your analytical skills to cell biology and microscopy research in close collaboration with experimental scientists. Your work will contribute directly to the quality, reproducibility and accessibility of the laboratory’s research data.

  Read more about the Faculty of Science at https://science.ku.dk/english/.

  Salary and conditions of employment
 This is a six-month fixed-term position. Employment will be under the collective agreement for academics employed by the Danish state (AC). Salary is determined by seniority, with the possibility of negotiating supplements based on qualifications. In addition to the basic salary, a monthly contribution to a pension fund is added (18.07% of the salary). Working hours average is 37 hours per week, with flexible working hours.

  Your application
 Please submit your application and supporting documents electronically through the University’s Job Portal by clicking “Apply for the position” at the bottom of the advertisement. The application deadline is 13 December 2026, and interviews will take place as soon as possible hereafter. 

  The University of Copenhagen seeks to reflect society and encourages applications from all candidates, irrespective of personal background.

  Contact information
 For further information, please contact Dimitrios Stamou, e-mail stamou@chem.ku.dk and tel. +45 3532 0479.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in cell free protein synthesis for prototyping and in vitro directed evolution - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Do you want to use synthetic biology to develop the next generation of sustainable materials? Join the Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) for a three-year, fully funded PhD project in cell-free protein synthesis. You will develop tools for rapid protein prototyping and in vitro directed evolution, expanding the design space of proteins for advanced materials.

Proteins combine precisely defined sequences with remarkable structural and functional diversity. Their programmable composition and capacity for self-assembly make them promising building blocks for materials with tailored properties. However, the natural repertoire of amino acids does not always provide the chemistry needed for demanding industrial applications.

Producing and testing new protein variants in living cells can be time-consuming and constrained by cellular physiology. Cell-free protein synthesis offers a flexible alternative, allowing direct control over reaction conditions and the available building blocks, while enabling the exploration of proteins that are difficult to produce in living cells.

During your PhD, you will harness these capabilities to develop high-throughput approaches for producing, screening and improving protein variants. By combining cell-free prototyping with in vitro directed evolution and exploring the incorporation of non-canonical amino acids, you will help create proteins with new chemical and material functionalities.

Your work will contribute directly to BRIGHT’s Mission 1A, Novel Biomanufacturing-Enabled Materials, which aims to develop PFAS-free biomaterials with defined composition, programmable chemistry and controlled assembly. Batteries provide the mission’s first proof-of-concept application, with a broader ambition to support advanced materials for energy technologies, coatings, electronics and other high-value applications.

You will help connect molecular design to experimental testing within the mission’s integrated biomanufacturing pipeline. In doing so, you will build expertise at the interface of synthetic biology, protein engineering and materials biotechnology, contributing to the development of sustainable alternatives to persistent fluorinated materials.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to develop high-throughput production and screening methods based on cell-free protein synthesis. You will genetically engineer bacteria and develop cell-free approaches for rapid protein prototyping and in vitro directed evolution. 

During the project, you will supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s students, collaborate closely with colleagues and coordinate with collaboration partners. These responsibilities require project-management skills, the ability to organise your own work and clear communication.

Lastly, you are expected to communicate scientific findings in international conferences as well as in high-impact scientific journals. Your primary tasks will be to:

• Genetic engineering of bacteria.
• Develop high-throughput cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) methods for producing and screening protein variants.
• Teach and supervise BSc and MSc student projects.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Key Selection Criteria

• Experience with cell free protein synthesis
• Experience with automated liquid handlers
• Hands-on experience in Synthetic Biology and Genetic Engineering is mandatory.
• Knowledge of cell metabolism and physiology, especially in environmental bacteria.
• You take initiative, think independently, organise your work and communicate constructively with colleagues.
• You work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute to shared research goals.
• Passionate about science and dedicated to the scientific project.

Do you want to help secure the critical minerals the green transition depends on – using biology instead of energy-hungry metallurgy? Then this PhD project is right in front of you. At DTU Bioengineering you will use advanced X-ray techniques at the new MicroMAX beamline at MAX IV in Lund to map minerals that contain rare earth elements (REEs) down to the atomic level. The project is part of the UQ-DTU Collaborative PhD Supervision Program: you will work in tandem with a PhD student at The University of Queensland (UQ) in Brisbane, Australia, who is discovering and engineering proteins that bind rare earth elements. Your overall focus will be the high-throughput structural characterisation of REE-bearing minerals from deposits in Greenland, Australia and South Africa. We are seeking an outstanding PhD fellow to join a cutting-edge research project exploring the links between environmental chemical exposures and reproductive health. By combining state-of-the-art exposomics, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and toxicological approaches, the project aims to identify chemicals and biological pathways that may contribute to adverse reproductive outcomes.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project will investigate how environmental chemical exposures influence female reproductive health through an integrated exposome-based approach. The candidate will characterize complex mixtures of environmental contaminants and endogenous biological responses using state-of-the-art LC-HRMS and non-target chemical analysis workflows. Research activities will include the development and application of analytical methods for profiling environmental and biological samples, advanced data processing and interpretation, and identification of exposure biomarkers and biologically relevant transformation products.

Cell-based assays will be used to investigate mechanisms linked to endocrine disruption, cellular metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, and reproductive function. Experimental PhD Project in Programmable Long-range Interactions of Cold Atoms

   

  NQCP invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in the experimental realization of controlled long-range atomic interactions.

  Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is establishing a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, we aim to establish an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that will drive research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to solutions for the quantum-classical control and readout interface, and all the way to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  Start date is April 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project
 We use ultra-cold atoms in optical traps to realize novel interaction-types that are useful in quantum simulation, computing, metrology and beyond.

  The PhD project will focus on developing accurate control of atomic interactions over long distances. You will be integrated in our existing team working on cavity-mediated interactions to realize light-defined control of the interaction strengths and programmable Hamiltonians. The daily work will be focused on designing, building and optimizing laser-based control infrastructure to realize the required level of atomic timing and light-shift control.

  As a PhD fellow in our research group you will become part of an ambitious and fast-moving research environment that pushes fundamental understanding of variable-range interactions in neutral atoms and apply that understanding to the development of computational capability.

  Who are we?
 At the NQCP we are enabling the realization of useful quantum computing which requires advanced architectures that are both fault-tolerant and scalable. In this effort we pursue four separate qubit modalities to carve out the best possible paths towards this goal. The Neutral Atoms group is pursuing the use of neutral atom qubits trapped in tweezers and optical lattices with controlled short-and long-range interactions. We work on

   	
• Long-range interactions using cavities and atomic transport 	
• Developing novel and fast read-write schemes in neutral atom platforms 	
• Programmable and holographic control of atomic energies.

 We are looking for highly motivated candidates that have a background in Atomic and Optical Physic, or Electrical Engineering. jobs.description:
Are you an experimental physicist or materials scientist who wants to build materials that do not exist in nature? Do you enjoy hands-on lab work, growing thin films and handling crystals only a few nanometres thick? Then join us at DTU Energy and help shape a new research field: oxide twistronics.

In the Section for Functional Oxides, we grow freestanding oxide membranes and stack them at chosen twist angles. In this project, funded by the Villum Investigator grant EUREKA, you will go a step further and build membrane structures with two or more twisted interfaces, each with its own twist angle and chemical termination. You will work closely with Professor Bharat Jalan's group at the University of Minnesota, where you will spend part of your PhD.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Joining two oxide crystals at a twist angle creates an interface with its own strain field, dislocation network and electronic structure. With a thick intermediate layer, two such interfaces should behave independently. As the layer gets thinner, their strain fields, distortions and electronic responses may begin to interact. You will also tune the bonding at each interface through the surface termination. The central question is whether two coupled interfaces give rise to collective phenomena that a single-interface bicrystal cannot show. You will start with SrTiO₃, fixed twist angles and terminations and a varying layer thickness, and then widen the range of configurations.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Grow SrTiO₃ films on sacrificial layers by pulsed laser deposition with controlled surface termination
• Release, transfer and stack freestanding membranes into structures with two or more twisted interfaces
• Grow films by hybrid molecular beam epitaxy during your research stay at the University of Minnesota
• Characterise structure, strain and interfaces with X-ray diffraction, scanning probe and electron microscopy
• Measure the electronic and functional response of the stacked structures
• Publish your results in international journals and present them at conferences

• An MSc in physics, materials science, chemistry, nanotechnology or a related field
